Detector design notes

A trustworthy similarity checker must explain its verdict, showing exactly which passages match and where they came from. Scores without evidence are worse than no scores at all, because they invite both false confidence and false accusation.

Modern detectors therefore combine several signals: word n-gram fingerprints survive reordering, sentence-level alignment captures light edits, and normalized token streams defeat character tricks. Finally, the report should separate quotation from appropriation, since citing a source honestly is the opposite of hiding one.

This fixture page exists so the web-check pipeline can be tested end to end without a real search provider: the mock provider returns its URL, the fetch endpoint extracts this article text, and the engine should attribute matching passages of the sample document to it.
